title: Owned external-packaging operating and capital policy
status: One prospective operating forecast, frozen before this companion equity output. No parameter grid or equity calculation performed here.
units: USD billions; annual normalized planning years; no wafer or package unit counts inferred
chronology: Existing base and funded-bull valuations and reverse cash hurdles were known before this policy. No equity output was inspected during this policy choice. Parameters were sent to root before annual operating arithmetic; no new value was calculated or used to select them.
preferred_direction: CPU recovery plus third-party packaging is the stronger operating LONG thesis. This is my preferred operating companion for evaluation, not a stock LONG recommendation before the fully funded cash/claim calculation. The prior high-confidence SHORT selection is withdrawn.

host_selection.rule: Use the existing funded-bull Products/Foundry/capital/WC path unchanged as the host. Do not also add the base-to-bull difference a second time.
host_selection.reason: Existing Ireland cleanrooms, reported plans to more than double its output in 2027, qualified Intel3/18A products and committed packaging demand improve the case for faster absorption. The host already pays additional $11B physical capital and $4B working capital in 2027–30 versus the constrained base.
host_selection.scope_of_Ireland_evidence: Reported doubling concerns Ireland output, not all Intel server units, accepted packages or consolidated revenue. I therefore retain host server-unit growth of 30/25/18/12% rather than substitute a doubling. Client contraction, package bottlenecks, rising D&A and 14A R&D remain in the host; no extra wafer-cost saving or product margin credit is added.
host_selection.source_quality: The concrete doubling statement and packaging margin/revenue aspirations are attributed CFO remarks from a third-party transcript of an issuer-verified event, not independently audio-verified. Other manufacturing readiness sources remain in the hashed physical-reuse ledger.

commercial_policy.program_formation: Own two large external customer program families reaching approximately $3B annual sales apiece plus $1B smaller programs by 2030. Customer count, allocation and size are assumptions, not undisclosed facts or assignments to Google/AWS/MediaTek.
commercial_policy.timing: The 2027 half-billion is recognized largely in the second half after equipment and qualification; no full-year billing on uncommissioned capacity is implied. The annual model does not claim actual customer acceptance dates.
commercial_policy.after2035: Both gross programs and the embedded baseline allowance grow 3% nominal annually; therefore the incremental revenue also grows 3%. Ongoing programs renew/refresh as a portfolio; no legal perpetual contract is asserted.
commercial_policy.revenue_scope: Third-party packaging/test revenue recognized by Intel, including materials Intel owns and recognizes gross where appropriate; customer-consigned logic/HBM value is not added. No internal Intel CPU packaging transfer, already-modeled Other DCAI custom silicon sale, or Intel16 legacy revenue is added again.
commercial_policy.margin: Program operating margins after direct depreciation, manufacturing payroll/materials, qualification, ongoing package R&D, support and program administration are -10/10/20/25% in 2027–30, 26% in 2031 and 27% from 2032. They are owned economic margins, below management’s attributed 30% aspiration, not observed project margins.
commercial_policy.incremental_corporate: Charge 1.5% of net incremental revenue for additional central functions and their ordinary cash-equivalent SBC. Program labor/R&D compensation is already in the program margin. Do not restore an SBC addback or additionally dilute for the same assumed cash-equivalent compensation.

baseline_overlap.existing_model_map: The host external-revenue series is Products plus Other; it has no explicit external Foundry sales series. That does NOT mean Foundry has zero external profit: its $3.5B 2030 profit and later 3%-of-Products allowance are aggregate and preserve existing external services. Other is Mobileye/IMS-type business, not a substitute for external Foundry.
baseline_overlap.rule: Treat the old aggregate Foundry allowance as already accommodating a smaller packaging opportunity with revenue 0.25/0.75/1.5/2B in 2027–30, then 3% nominal growth. Deduct the POSITIVE profit of that allowance at the same program margin from gross program EBIT. Do not reverse a hypothetical prior startup loss: overlap is max(0, allowance times margin). Add only gross sales minus this revenue allowance to displayed consolidated external sales.
baseline_overlap.2030_identity: Gross program revenue7B less embedded2B gives5B incremental sales. Gross program EBIT1.75B less embedded0.50B gives1.25B incremental segment profit; central/SBC0.075B reduces net incremental EBIT to1.175B. Host Foundry3.5B is therefore not claimed internal-only.
baseline_overlap.rationale: A small program of roughly $2B annual sales is a reasonable explicit reservation within a substantial old aggregate recovery allowance. Its $0.5B profit is about one seventh of host2030 Foundry profit. This is an owned attribution to prevent full stacking, not a reconstructed disclosure or a uniquely identified amount.
baseline_overlap.capital_overlap: No existing PPE is reclaimed as cash or credited to this companion. The separate capital schedule funds only the incremental program capacity above that shadow allowance; the host retains its own entire capital and WC budget. Do not fund gross7B plus also separately fund embedded2B.
baseline_overlap.profit_savings_overlap: No additional fixed-cost absorption benefit is credited on the host’s wafers, internal packages or process R&D. Program margin bears its own directly attributable costs; shared customer/platform improvements remain inside the conservative overlap treatment.

capital_and_cash_policy.scope: Wholly Intel-owned additional back-end equipment, facility fit-out/expansion and qualification-related capital. Distinct funded capacity prevents external programs from silently consuming tools/substrates already needed by the bullish CPU ramp. Capital is paid in cash; no upfront free existing plant, unannounced lease funding, customer prepayment, partner contribution, extra NCI reserve or extra AMIC credit.
capital_and_cash_policy.initial_DA: For the initial2027–30 additions only, use80% equipment depreciated straight-line over7 years and20% facility/fit-out over20 years, with half-year in-service convention. All four years precede the first modeled retirement. These are owned book-life assumptions, not verified equipment contracts.
capital_and_cash_policy.post2030_DA: Transition to aggregate incremental D&A equal to13/14/15/15.5/16% of incremental revenue in2031–35, then16%. This REPLACES the initial cohort calculation after2030 and includes depreciation of inherited and new program assets; never add the initial-cohort D&A again. It is an explicit portfolio normalization, not an exact seven-year replacement timetable.
capital_and_cash_policy.WC: Incremental net operating working-capital stock equals15% of incremental sales; annual cash use is its change. No negative customer-funded float or later release windfall is assumed.
capital_and_cash_policy.post2030_growth_reinvestment: Incremental sales-to-net-operating-capital is1.0, INCLUDING working capital. Total net investment equals change in incremental revenue divided by1.0. Gross physical capex equals D&A plus that net investment minus WC cash use.
capital_and_cash_policy.replacement: Post2030 gross capex includes a recurring renewal/maintenance allowance equal to normalized D&A plus physical growth investment. This funds continuing equipment renewal rather than capitalizing startup profits with no replacement. Annual replacement bunching is smoothed; actual qualification/tool retirement dates could change cash timing and must not be claimed validated by this normalization.
capital_and_cash_policy.mature_economics: From2036 revenue, EBIT, D&A, capex and WC cash all grow3%. At16% D&A and1.0 incremental capital turnover, gross capex is about18.48% of that year’s incremental revenue, with the remaining net investment exactly funding3% nominal sales growth. Positive growth is not free.
capital_and_cash_policy.integration_guard: Add these capital/WC/D&A rows directly to the host. Do NOT also run incremental packaging sales through the host0.60 capital-turnover rule, or add a second maintenance/ROIC charge.
capital_and_cash_policy.financing_interest: Physical capital excludes capitalized interest. Root/finance may charge actual new financing interest once in treasury if required; none is hidden in this operating schedule.
capital_and_cash_policy.tax_and_claims: Root retains its existing tax, finite credit, debt, lease, NCI and claim policies, recalculating tax/liquidity if the changed cash path requires it. No incremental government credit or customer-funded cash is credited here.

committed_packaging.use: Supports committed demand and2027 revenue conversion, not exact program count/size.

conference.locator: EMIB-T discussion and Ireland capacity discussion
conference.use: Attributed management expectations: multibillion annual sales per customer,40% gross/30% operating margin, lower capital intensity than front-end, Ireland output expansion. Not audio-verified or an enforceable minimum.

amkor_sanity.locator: Quarterly results, business outlook, Selected Operating Data
amkor_sanity.use: Amkor Q3 sales1.991B, operating margin11.3%, depreciation in gross cost8.6% of sales, and FY2026capex guidance2.5B. Its broad advanced-product mix is not equivalent to Intel EMIB. It cautions that27% Intel program margins require differentiated service, and expansion can require substantial capital; it does not calibrate the chosen coefficients.

counterarguments_and_controls: The strongest downside is delayed qualification or commodity-like customer bargaining: Intel’s realized packaging margin may remain much closer to broad OSAT economics than27%, while equipment and customer support costs are already committed.
The strongest upside is more than two large customers, reuse of already-paid suitable tools, or stronger sustained margins. None is added as an unpriced free option in these rows.

Existing packaging opportunity overlap cannot be uniquely measured. The explicit2B-sales/0.5B-profit2030 reservation prevents treating the entire modeled Foundry recovery as internal, but remains an important attribution judgment.

Output doubling in one Ireland process cannot certify the host’s all-company server units or substrate availability. If finished package delivery lags, both the host and this companion can be simultaneously too optimistic.

Portfolio D&A/maintenance smoothing does not reproduce a physical tool-vintage ledger. The annual capital budget is real spending in the forecast; the timing of future refresh is an unresolved cash-cycle risk, not a zero-cost assumption.
